headline: High: Authelia can expose sensitive auth context to Cognee via broad egress and shared OAuth/LLM-backed workflows, while default interaction paths also create prompt-injection and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can ingest and forward auth-related content through OIDC/ForwardAuth, and Cognee processes documents/workflows with session memory. A shared filesystem is not documented, so the strongest documented pathway is indirect: content from Authelia can be fed into Cognee and treated as trusted context. That is enough for a medium risk, not high, because no direct parser bridge is shown.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs user-controlled claims or headers into a workflow that Cognee ingests as context, injection is possible.
IF Cognee treats imported documents or workflow text as instructions without provenance checks, malicious content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all Authelia-derived text before ingestion.
Require manual review of any Authelia output before Cognee consumes it.
Strip executable-looking directives from imported text.
Use a separate staging workspace for imports.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. Even without a documented shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive identity or support data from Authelia-adjacent flows into Cognee's memory/workflows and then out over network egress. Because the exact transport is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Authelia is used in front of systems carrying personal or finance data, that data can enter the pair's processing path.
IF Cognee stores imported support or identity data in session memory, later outputs may reveal it to downstream consumers.
mitigations: Limit Authelia to non-sensitive tenants.
Disable import of personal or finance data into Cognee.
Review and redact auth logs before indexing.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is not runnable and has no filesystem-write capability documented, while Cognee supports multiple instances with session-scoped memory and CLI use. There is no documented overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource, so direct conflict is unlikely. The remaining risk is limited to coordination mistakes if both are pointed at the same external service.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external backend or API namespace, state conflicts can occur.
IF Cognee instances share a session or tenant identifier, concurrent updates may overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign distinct tenants or namespaces.
Serialize writes through one operator.
Check for duplicate session IDs before running.
Use read-only mode for one agent.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication decisions and Cognee can store decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If Cognee consumes Authelia outputs as authoritative context, a mistaken auth decision can cascade into downstream workflow or support actions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction exists in default-style integrations, but the blast radius is not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF Cognee ingests Authelia-authored decisions without verification, errors can propagate.
IF downstream workflows act on stored decisions, a bad auth signal can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require human verification for auth-derived decisions.
Tag Authelia outputs as untrusted until checked.
Keep a rollback copy of imported records.
Limit downstream automation on imported decisions.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer with no touched data classes listed, while Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history. If EU or regulated personal data flows through Authelia into Cognee, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed from Authelia into Cognee, compliance obligations apply to both systems.
IF Cognee retains imported support or finance data longer than the source policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Block regulated data from non-approved flows.
Document retention periods for both systems.
Review vendor terms for residency and DPA coverage.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement.
